items.title: Every frontier town seats its wonder inside its wall ring
items.brief:
What is wrong today
Take the first 60 frontier towns, frontierSettlementSeedsNear(0, 0, 1500).slice(0, 60), and their plans, settlementPlan(getRealmDefinition(id)). In 15 of them the wonder stands 59 to 73 m from the centre, outside the wall ring (plan.wallRadius is 52):
- all six towns with the grid 'blocks' plan style (Suncoast and Clayborn, for example frontier_0_1 Fernstead);
- nine towns with the 'river' terrace style (Riverfolk and Reedfolk).
The tallest landmark then stands alone in the fields instead of dominating the core.

Required behaviour
For every one of those 60 towns, plan.named.get('wonder-1') is defined and its PlanSlot.radius is less than plan.wallRadius. (The 60 include at least one 'blocks' town and at least one 'river' town, and both styles must pass.)

Every existing plan invariant still holds, for all 60 towns:
- The wonder-1 parcel still holds the whole wonder: Math.min(plot.w, plot.d) of that parcel is at least Math.max(BUILDING_KIND_DEFS.wonder.w, BUILDING_KIND_DEFS.wonder.d) (10 m).
- plan.style is CULTURE_PLAN of the town's culture (getRealmDefinition(id).cultureId).
- plan.homes.length is at least 100.
- The wall ring keeps its towers and gates: among the keys of plan.named, exactly 2 start with 'gatehouse-', at least 4 start with 'watchtower-' and at least 30 start with 'wall-' (today these towns have 2, 5 to 12, and 38 to 48). 'keep-1' is present.
- The skyline rule: at least 40 of the 60 towns have wonder-1 radius < 48, and at least 55 have keep-1 radius < 35.

In every 'blocks' and 'river' town among the 60, no two parcels overlap and no street runs through a parcel:
- The parcels are every entry of plan.homes, plan.crafts, plan.market, plan.farm and plan.wells, plus the distinct values of plan.named (each a PlanSlot).
- A point p is inside parcel s shrunk by k when |dx*cos(r) - dz*sin(r)| < s.plot.w / 2 - k and |dx*sin(r) + dz*cos(r)| < s.plot.d / 2 - k, where dx = p.x - s.x, dz = p.z - s.z and r = s.rotation. A parcel's corners are its centre offset by (u*hw*cos(r) + v*hd*sin(r), -u*hw*sin(r) + v*hd*cos(r)) for u, v in {-1, 1}, with hw = plot.w / 2 and hd = plot.d / 2.
- Two parcels overlap when a corner of either is inside the other shrunk by 0.05. A pair of parcels that are both in the 'wall' district (s.district), where either has plot.w === 3 (a tower capping a curtain segment), may overlap.
- No point of any street in plan.streets (street.points) is inside any parcel with no shrink, the wonder-1 parcel included. Gatehouse parcels are exempt, since the main road runs through them.

Existing tests that pass today must keep passing (plans stay deterministic, and the hamlet-to-city kind mix, docks where towns meet the river, the keep near the square and the saved-lot migration rules are unchanged).

items.title: Towns raised to a population house everyone (no campers packing the plaza)
The missing-axe favour stops misleading new players
items.brief:
What is wrong today
Rowan's lost-axe spot (the interaction point with id 'tool') is offered as a 'Rowan's lost axe · Help' target before the player has accepted the favour. The journal's 'Mark on the map' for a favour always leads to the favour's work spot, so a new player is sent to the axe spot, and tapping it there only gives a generic refusal until they happen to talk to Rowan.

Required behaviour
1. For a village state s, interactionPoints(s) does not include a point with id 'tool' while s.requests.tool is 'new'. It includes it once the favour is 'accepted', and no longer includes it once the axe is found (s.requestProgress.toolFound is true) or once the favour is 'ready' or 'complete' (as today).
2. Export requestDestination(s: VillageState, id: RequestId) from src/village/interactions.ts (the module that already exports interactionPoints). It returns, as a string destination id, where 'Mark on the map' should lead for that favour:
   - while the favour is 'new', 'ready' or 'complete': the workplace of the neighbour who offers it: tool -> 'timber' (Rowan), cart -> 'grain', garden -> 'mira', introduction -> 'workshop';
   - while it is 'accepted': where the work happens: tool -> 'tool', cart -> 'cart', garden -> 'garden', introduction -> 'gathering';
   - except that the accepted tool favour returns 'timber' once s.requestProgress.toolFound is true.
   The journal's 'Mark on the map' button for each favour leads to requestDestination(s, id).
3. The 'find' step keeps requiring an accepted favour: on a new game (s = createVillage()), actVillage(s, { type: 'request', requestId: 'tool', step: 'find' }) returns a state whose requestProgress.toolFound is false and whose requests.tool is 'new'.

The favour steps are unchanged: step 'accept' makes a favour 'accepted'; for the tool favour, 'find' sets requestProgress.toolFound, 'return' makes it 'ready' and 'claim' makes it 'complete'.

Existing tests that pass today must keep passing.

items.title: Saving never loses the only legacy save, and autosave stops redoing work
items.brief:
What is wrong today
saveVillage(state, storage) has two faults.
1) Data loss. When storage is too full for the save to be written at all (setItem throws a quota error), saveVillage returns false, and a player migrating from an older save finds their legacy save keys ('alder.village.v3', 'alder.village.v3.backup', the v2 and v1 keys) gone afterwards. Their only save is lost.
2) Slow autosaves. With four grown cities each autosave takes about 93 ms, even when the stored primary is exactly the payload this session wrote last time.

Interface
saveVillage(state, storage?) and saveStorageFull() are the existing exports, with VILLAGE_SAVE_KEY (the primary) and VILLAGE_BACKUP_KEY (the backup). storage can be any Storage-like object (getItem, setItem, removeItem, key, length); a full store throws from setItem with an error whose name is 'QuotaExceededError'. The payload is the exact string saveVillage writes to VILLAGE_SAVE_KEY for a state. The legacy keys are 'alder.village.v3', 'alder.village.v3.backup', 'alder.village.v2', 'alder.village.v2.backup', 'alder.village.v1' and 'alder.village.v1.backup'.

Required behaviour
- Whenever saveVillage returns false, every legacy key that existed before the call is still present with its original value. For example, with a few hundred characters of legacy saves stored and a quota one character smaller than the new payload, nothing can be written: saveVillage returns false and every legacy value is intact.
- When the new payload fits on its own, saving still succeeds as today: saveVillage returns true, VILLAGE_SAVE_KEY holds the payload, and saveStorageFull() returns true when the backup had to be dropped (for example with a quota of 1.5 times the payload length and an 'alder.village.v3' key present).
- An ordinary save with enough space still leaves at most one of the six legacy keys, and saveStorageFull() returns false.
- After a successful save to a storage, if that storage's VILLAGE_SAVE_KEY value has not changed since, the next saveVillage call to that storage makes no call to JSON.parse at all (on the stored primary or on anything else). It still moves that previous primary into VILLAGE_BACKUP_KEY and writes the new payload to VILLAGE_SAVE_KEY.
- A corrupt primary is never copied into the backup. If something else replaced the stored primary after this session's save (for example with '{broken', with the payload's last character changed, or with only its first half), the next save still returns true, writes the new payload to VILLAGE_SAVE_KEY, and leaves VILLAGE_BACKUP_KEY holding something other than the corrupt string.

Existing tests that pass today must keep passing.

items.title: Morning letters carry only news since the previous morning, never repeats
items.brief:
What is wrong today
At every morning bell the game toasts up to two 'letters' drawn from the event logs. The same lines come back every morning whether or not they were already delivered, so 'Welcome to Alder. Mira's roof is waiting on timber…' arrives again every day. A line can also be toasted twice in the same morning (the founding-stake offer appears as its own toast and again as a letter).

Interface
For a village state s, toasts are the entries of s.moments with kind 'toast'; a toast's text is its line with the first letter capitalised, as today. Event lines are Alder's own s.events, and '<Town name>: <line>' for each line of a realm settlement's events (s.realm.settlements[id].events, with the name REALM_DEFS[id].name). The morning bell rings at 06:00; stepVillage advances the game.

Required behaviour
- A morning's letter toasts carry only event lines that appeared since the previous morning bell.
- Letters are still toasted at the morning bell itself, in the same simulation step as the bell banner: the single stepVillage tick that crosses 06:00 carries them.
- If nothing new happened, that morning pushes no letter toast. The bell banner and other features' own dawn moments are unaffected.
- A new event line added between two mornings (for example 'The storehouse reached tier 2.' appended to s.events) is toasted exactly once, on the next morning, and not on the morning after.
- No morning pushes two toasts with identical text.
- Letters keep today's selection: routine lines starting 'Collected ', 'Took ' or 'Stored ' are never letters; Alder's own lines come first, newest first, then other towns' lines with their name prefix; at most two letter toasts per morning.

Existing tests that pass today must keep passing. If your change adds state that an existing test pins by its exact shape, you may extend that assertion to include the new field; do not weaken or delete any other assertion.

items.title: Buckets can be filled at wells, not only at the river
items.brief:
What is wrong today
An empty bucket fills only at the river. The bucket's fill step, actVillage(state, { type: 'feature', feature: 'wander', action: { type: 'bucket', step: 'fill' } }), refuses everywhere else with 'Fill it at the water's edge.', even when the player is standing right beside a well. Yet the player-built Well piece promises 'Water close to home; buckets for fires', and towns dig wells of their own.

Required behaviour
An empty bucket (state.features.wander.bucket === 'empty') becomes 'full' when the player (state.player x, z) stands within 2.4 m, measured horizontally, of the centre of any of these:
(a) a standing Well piece the player built: an entry of kind 'well' in state.features.building.pieces with condition > 0. Its centre is the centre of its cell: cell x + 0.5, cell z + 0.5.
(b) a completed well lot in any discovered realm settlement (any town in state.realm.settlements): a lot with buildingType 'well' and tier >= 1, centred at the lot's x, z.
(c) a completed well commission in the player's own town: an entry in state.features.claimTown.town.commissions with kind 'well' and complete true, centred at its x, z.

These do not count: a knocked-down well piece (condition 0), a well lot at tier 0, and a well commission that is not complete. Next to one of those, with no river in reach, the fill is refused and the bucket stays 'empty'.

Unchanged
- Filling at the river's edge works as before.
- Anywhere with no river and no counting well in reach, the fill is still refused and the bucket stays 'empty'.
- Taking a bucket from the store, pouring a full bucket, and a bucket's effect against fire all work as before.

items.title: Residents gossip about your escorts and caravan crates
items.brief:
What is wrong today
When the player escorts a caravan or has a crate commissioned, the caravans feature logs a caravan deed in state.features.caravans.deeds (entries { kind: 'escort' | 'commission', settlementId, at }). Residents never hear about it. No gossip deed appears in state.features.council.gossip.deeds, and no resident ever mentions trade or caravan work. Gossip has a 'trade' deed kind, and Nell cares about trade news more than anything, but no 'trade' deed is ever recorded.

Required behaviour
- Each new caravan deed for a realm town (its settlementId is a realm id such as 'willow' or 'cairn') becomes exactly one gossip deed in state.features.council.gossip.deeds within a second of simulated time. For example, after one stepVillage(state, 1.5) following the caravan deed being logged, the gossip deed is there. The same caravan deed is never turned into a second gossip deed, however long the game runs afterwards.
- That gossip deed has kind 'trade'. Its place is the town's display name: 'Willowbank' for 'willow', 'Cairnstead' for 'cairn'.
- The lines residents say about it, barkToPlayer(deed, npcId) and overheardLine(deed, speaker), contain that town's name. They contain no unfilled '{…}' slot and never the text 'undefined'.
- When such a fresh trade deed is the only news, pickGossip(state, state.features.council.gossip, 'nell') returns that deed.
- Caravan deeds already logged when the game was saved are not reported again after saveVillage then loadVillage, however long the loaded game runs. Gossip deeds recorded before the save are still there after the load, as today.

Unchanged
Every other kind of gossip deed, and the lines for those kinds, work as before. The existing council and gossip tests keep passing.

items.title: Settlers who want a home in their own style accept a piece-built home in that style
items.brief:
What is wrong today
Two authored settlers, Petrok (Clayborn) and Sefa (Suncoast), want 'a home in their own style'. In a player town of another culture neither can ever be satisfied. That stays true even after the player learns their culture's building style and builds them a home from pieces in it. Their verdict on such a home is the same as on the same home in the town's style, and 'style' is still the want they name.

Required behaviour
1. The PieceSite type gains an optional field culture?: CultureId. It is the culture style a piece-built place was built in.
2. The object returned by homeFacts(town, id, …) gains a field style: CultureId, the style the home is built in:
   - a piece-built home whose piece site has a culture: that culture;
   - a piece-built home whose site has no culture, and every commissioned house: the town's own culture (town.culture).
   When stepClaimTown(state, ctx) receives ctx.pieceSites and one of them is a house with a culture, homeFacts for that home (by the site's id) reports that culture as style.
3. In the running game (stepVillage), a home the player builds from pieces inside their town carries the style its pieces were placed in. Each placed piece records the building style that was selected when it was placed, as that culture's index in CULTURE_IDS. So homeFacts for that home's piece site in state.features.claimTown.town.pieceSites reports that culture as style. When a home's pieces are all in one style, that style is the home's. How a home of mixed styles is classed is up to you.
4. localVerdict(def, facts, town, …) treats a settler's 'style' want as met exactly when facts.style equals the settler's own culture (def.culture). So for a settler who wants 'style':
   - a home in the settler's own style: 'style' is not the returned want, and the score is higher than for the same home in any other style;
   - a home in another style, including the town's own style when that differs from the settler's culture: the returned want is 'style'.

Unchanged
Every other want and every other part of the verdict score work as before. Existing tests that pass today must keep passing.

items.title: Repairing damage and defending against threats earn standing and town help
items.brief:
What is wrong today
The reputation ladder has 'repaired' and 'rescued' deed kinds, each with an authored verdict and 12 growth help (state.realm.settlements[id].help). Nothing the player does against threats ever earns either one. Finishing a repair of storm damage, carrying home a bundle dropped by thieves, or standing guard until a threat passes records no deed with the town, and the town's growth help does not move. Only the flat state.reputation number goes up.

Required behaviour
This applies to threats and damage at the home village's own buildings, for example the village kiln or the communal store. Those count as realm 'alder'.
- Repair: the player finishes repairing damage with actVillage(state, { type: 'feature', feature: 'threats', action: { type: 'repair', damageId } }). A 'repaired' deed is recorded for 'alder'. Only the repair action that completes the repair counts. A repair action that leaves work still to do records nothing and gives no help.
- Dropped bundle: the player carries home a thieves' dropped bundle (damage with cause 'thieves', recovered with the same repair action). A 'rescued' deed is recorded for 'alder' instead.
- Guarded threat: a threat resolves because the player guarded it fully (its guard >= guardNeeded). A 'rescued' deed is recorded for 'alder'.
- Each such deed appears in state.features.reputation.standings.alder.deeds with realmId 'alder' and its kind. It raises state.realm.settlements.alder.help by 12.
- These record no deed and give no help: damage that residents mend on their own (self-repair), and a threat turned away only by lamps without the player guarding it fully.

Unchanged
Everything else the threats feature does on these events is unchanged: its moments, stock movements, the flat reputation bonus, the held count and the removal of finished damage. The existing threats tests keep passing.

items.title: Map overlay shows trade routes between towns
items.brief:
What is wrong today
The map overlay's links, historyMapLinks(state, townIds), show only two things: diplomatic stances between towns (pact, alliance, rivalry, dispute, embargo) and each town's internal supply chains. The owner asked for history to show on the map through 'map overlays for routes and alliances'. Trade routes between towns never appear, even between towns that trade all the time.

Required behaviour
- MapLink's kind gains 'route'. LINK_STYLE gains a 'route' entry with a non-empty stroke colour string and a width greater than 0, like the other entries.
- historyMapLinks(state, townIds) returns exactly one link of kind 'route' for every pair of towns where at least one of the two is in townIds, and either of these holds:
  - the pair has traded: their history relation, state.features.history.rel[pairKey(a, b)], has total > 0;
  - a merchant from one of them is on a trade trip to the other right now: a worker of a realm settlement in state.realm.settlements whose task.kind is 'trade' and whose task.partnerId is the other town.
- A route runs centre to centre: from and to are the two towns' centres, getRealmDefinition(id).center as [x, z], in either order.
- A route's label contains both towns' names (getRealmDefinition(id).name, for example 'Alder North', 'Willowbank', 'Cairnstead'). It also contains the relation's total traded as a number: 0 when the pair has no relation or has not traded yet.
- A pair gets at most one route, however many merchants are on the road between them in either direction, and whether or not it has also traded.
- A pair whose relation has a stance (anything other than 'none') already gets its stance link. It gets no route link as well.
- Pairs that have never traded and have no merchant on the road between them get no route.
- Pairs where neither town is in townIds get no route.
- Every link id in the result stays unique.

Unchanged
Stance links and supply-chain links are drawn as before. The existing history and village map tests keep passing.

items.title: Signature caravans count as trade for diplomacy and the chronicle
items.brief:
What is wrong today
Realm merchants now carry most goods between towns as signature loads (each culture's SIGNATURE_GOODS good), delivered into the partner town's signature store. The history feature does not count those deliveries as trade:
- they never raise a relation's traded or total;
- they never feed the diplomacy review;
- they never appear in any town's chronicle.
In one run with no ordinary trade, the three core towns exchanged 25 signature units in 45 minutes. Every relation's total stayed 0, and Alder–Willowbank drifted to -11.5 goodwill.

Required behaviour
- Each signature delivery from town A to town B adds its amount to the history relation between them, state.features.history.rel[pairKey(A, B)]. It raises traded and total by that same amount, at the same moment. The relation is created if it does not exist yet. Crediting may lag the delivery by a few seconds of simulated time, but never more than 10 s. Every delivered unit is credited exactly once.
- Outside a diplomacy review, a relation's total and traded always move together, by the same amount.
- The receiving town's chronicle, state.features.history.towns[B].entries, records the first signature delivery from each partner town as an entry of kind 'trade'. The entry's text:
  - contains the good's SIGNATURE_GOODS label word for word, whatever the amount (for example 'carved beams', even for a single beam);
  - names the sending town by its realm name, getRealmDefinition(A).name (for example 'Cairnstead').
- This holds in a game where nothing but signature caravans moves goods between towns, for example when every realm town's treasury is 0, over at least 45 simulated minutes.

Unchanged
Ordinary resource trade is credited and chronicled as before. The existing history, economy and caravans tests keep passing. A saved game still loads and carries on, and trade credited before the save is not credited again after the load.

items.title: Resource amounts read correctly in the singular ('1 plank', not '1 planks')
items.brief:
What is wrong today
The 'plural with 1' bug was fixed only for signature goods. Resource amounts still read wrong in several places:
- threat repair needs, from bagText: 'It needs mending: 1 timber, 1 planks'. Tiles show as '1 tiles' or '2 tiles', where everywhere else the game calls them roof tiles.
- your town's building-site needs, from needsText: '1 planks'.
- filled orders, from goodLabel(good, amount): 'Order filled … 1 planks'. goodLabel('planks', 1) returns 'planks'.
- building-piece crafting refuses with 'Needs 1 planks.', and rebuilding a knocked-down piece refuses with 'Needs 1 planks to rebuild.'.

Required behaviour
- Export resourceAmount(amount: number, resource: ResourceId): string from src/village/content.ts. It returns the amount, a space, and the resource's display label in lower case. Planks and roof tiles are count nouns and take the singular for exactly one: '1 plank', '2 planks', '1 roof tile', '3 roof tiles'. Every other resource is a mass noun and does not change: '1 timber', '5 bread', '1 stone', '2 flour', '1 clay', '1 grain'.
- bagText(bag) and needsText(commission) write each amount this way. They keep their current resource order and separators. For example:
  - bagText({ timber: 1, planks: 1 }) === '1 timber, 1 plank'
  - bagText({ tiles: 2 }) === '2 roof tiles'
  - bagText({ tiles: 1 }) === '1 roof tile'
  - bagText({ tiles: 1, stone: 3 }) === '3 stone, 1 roof tile'
  - a house commission still owing one plank has a needsText containing '1 plank' and not '1 planks'.
- goodLabel(good, amount) uses the singular resource label when amount is 1, and the plural otherwise:
  - goodLabel('planks', 1) === 'plank' and goodLabel('planks', 2) === 'planks';
  - goodLabel('tiles', 1) === 'roof tile' and goodLabel('tiles', 4) === 'roof tiles';
  - goodLabel('timber', 1) === 'timber'.
  Signature goods still return signatureLabel(good, amount) for every amount.
- The building-piece refusals from reduceBuilding read:
  - 'Needs 1 plank.' when crafting a wall with only 1 of its 2 planks;
  - 'Needs 1 plank to rebuild.' when repairing a knocked-down wall with no planks.
  Any existing test pinned to the old '1 planks' wording is updated to the new wording.

Unchanged
The threats, claim-town, economy and building test suites pass.

items.title: Threats at your own town take and mend with your town's store, not Alder's
items.brief:
Today a threat that lands on one of your own town's buildings settles its goods against Alder's communal store. Thieves at your town's storehouse carry off goods from Alder's store (state.stock) and leave your town's store (state.features.claimTown.town.stock) untouched; bringing their dropped bundle home puts the goods into Alder's store. Storm or fire damage to your town's buildings that you leave alone is mended after a day ('Bran's crew mended ... while you were busy') out of Alder's store. Alder's ledger (state.ledger) books all of it.

Required, for threat targets that belong to your town (target id 'claimTown:' followed by the site's commission id, for example 'claimTown:player_1:storehouse:3'):
- When thieves at your town are not turned away, the goods come out of your town's store by the rule Alder uses today: the two goods it holds most of, each up to 2 + stages lost (DamageRecord.stagesLost) and never more than it holds. The damage record's cache (DamageRecord.cache) is exactly what left your town's store.
- Completing that dropped bundle's repair (actVillage with {type: 'feature', feature: 'threats', action: {type: 'repair', damageId}}, standing at the bundle) removes the record and puts the cache back into your town's store.
- Damage to your town's buildings that reaches its selfRepairAt is mended from your town's store when that store holds every remaining need: those goods leave it and the record is removed. If it does not, the record stays and its selfRepairAt moves later, to be tried again.
- None of this changes Alder's state.stock or state.ledger, even when Alder's store could pay.
- Threats at Alder's own targets (for example thieves at 'storage', the communal store) behave exactly as today.

A threat can be put in place as an ActiveThreat in state.features.threats.active (it resolves on the first stepVillage tick at or after its endAt), and damage as DamageRecord entries in state.features.threats.damage; both are existing exported types. The existing threats tests must keep passing.

items.title: What you build is solid for everyone
items.brief:
The simulation's own collision ignores what the player builds. After you place walls, fences, wells or stalls, walkable(x, z) and playerWalkable(x, z) still report those spots as open, so Alder's residents and realm workers walk straight through them: findRoute from one side of a fence line to the other returns a straight line through it. Pieces block only the player's own movement, and only in the browser. Your own town's finished buildings block nobody, the player included. A bridge span laid over the river is crossable for the player only.

Required, once the simulation has stepped (stepVillage) with the pieces or sites in place:
- Building pieces live in state.features.building.pieces as PieceTuple entries: [index in PIECE_IDS, cell x, cell z, rotation 0-3, style variant, condition 0-2]. Edge pieces sit on a cell boundary: rotation 0 or 2 on the cell's north line along x, 1 or 3 on its west line along z.
- walkable(x, z) and playerWalkable(x, z) both return false wherever pieceBlocks(pieces, x, z) (its default radius) is true, that is, near a standing piece (condition above 0) whose PIECE_DEFS entry has blocks: true. Doors, gates, floors, paths, garden beds, beds, benches, lamps, signs and knocked-down pieces (condition 0) stay open. A piece that is knocked down or taken away opens its spot again after the next step.
- A standing bridge span (condition above 0) makes the centre of its cell walkable (both functions true) even where inRiver is true there. A knocked-down span does not.
- Every finished site of your own town (entries of state.features.claimTown.town.commissions with complete: true and kind house, workshop, storehouse, hall, marvel, well or shrine) makes both functions false within 0.6 x COMMISSION_DEFS[kind].radius of the site's centre. Campfires, bedrolls, lamp posts and unfinished sites do not block. A point more than COMMISSION_DEFS[kind].radius + 0.5 m from every site is not affected by them.
- Take a straight fence line at least 6 m long on open ground, and two points 2 m either side of its middle. findRoute(from, to) between them returns a non-empty route ending at the destination, and segmentWalkable holds for each leg, from the start through every route point, so no leg crosses the fence.

Existing navigation, terrain, collision, building and simulation tests must keep passing.

items.title: Your town's sites and the places you built never land on each other
items.brief:
Your town's commission sites ignore what you built from pieces, and pieces ignore your sites. commissionBlockedReason(s, 'house', x, z) returns '' for a spot on top of a home you built (one of town.pieceSites), so Mark site and typed orders can put a House over it. Nothing stops a marked site or a typed order from covering your walls and fences. 'A lamp by the well' anchors to the banner when the town's only well is one you built. Building pieces can be placed inside a marked site.

Required:
- commissionBlockedReason(s, kind, x, z) returns a non-empty reason when the new site would overlap one of s.town.pieceSites, by the rule it already uses between sites: centre distance less than COMMISSION_DEFS[kind].radius + COMMISSION_DEFS[site.kind].radius. All its existing reasons stay.
- Marking a site (feature 'claimTown', {type: 'commission', kind}) and giving a typed order (feature 'council', {type: 'order', text}, for example text 'a house', standing in your town) never create a site that commissionBlockedReason refuses. They also never create one whose centre is closer than COMMISSION_DEFS[kind].radius to the pieceCenter of a standing piece that blocks walking (PIECE_DEFS entry with blocks: true, condition above 0). Knocked-down pieces (condition 0) do not count, and with no standing pieces in the way sites go where they go today. When a spot they would pick is ruled out by a piece site or a standing piece, they still create the site, at the next spot they would try, as they already do when a spot clashes with another site. This holds for pieces that were in place when the simulation last stepped. The typed-order box and the orders Jev is asked to choose between offer a site order only when such a site could go down.
- In a typed order, an anchor word ('by', 'near', 'next') that names a well, shrine, workshop or house anchors to your town's commissioned site of that kind; when the town has no commission of that kind, it anchors to the first piece site of that kind in town.pieceSites. With only a piece-built well, siteFor(ct, 'lamp', 'a lamp by the well') returns a spot within 8 m of that well; once the town also has a well commission, the spot is within 8 m of the commissioned well.
- Placing a building piece (feature 'building', {type: 'place', x, z, piece, rotation}) is refused, and actVillage returns the same state object, when the placed piece's centre (pieceCenter of the snapped placement) lies within COMMISSION_DEFS[kind].radius of the centre of any of your town's commissions except the campfire and the bedroll, finished or not. Elsewhere, including beside the campfire, placement works as today.

Pieces are PieceTuple entries of state.features.building.pieces: [index in PIECE_IDS, cell x, cell z, rotation 0-3, style variant, condition 0-2]. Places you built from pieces are Commission entries in state.features.claimTown.town.pieceSites; pieceSite({id, kind, x, z}) makes one. Existing claimTown, council and building tests must keep passing.

items.title: The map marks what needs you
items.brief:
The map shows buildings, residents, roads and relations, but nothing that asks for the player. It does not show a building stalled on a milestone gate, damage waiting for repair, a bundle the thieves dropped, the threat that is coming, or the caravans on the road (realm merchants or your own crates). Yet gates are meant to show at their site, threats and repairs to be found, and caravans to be seen.

Required: export villageMapMarkers(state: VillageState, bounds: MapBounds): MapMarker[] from src/village/villageMapModel.ts, with MapMarker = {id: string; kind: 'stall' | 'damage' | 'threat' | 'caravan'; x: number; z: number; label: string}. It returns these markers, but only those whose point is inside bounds (mapContains(bounds, x, z)):
- one 'stall' marker per active lot of any known realm settlement (state.realm.settlements) whose milestone gate is still short (gateShortfall(settlement, lot) is non-empty), at the lot's workpoint, with id 'stall:' + settlement id + ':' + lot id, and a label that starts 'Waiting for' and names each missing good as its amount, a space, then signatureLabel(good, amount). A lot that is not active, or whose gate goods are all on hand, has no stall marker.
- one 'damage' marker per record in state.features.threats.damage, at its x and z, with id 'damage:' + record id, and label 'Dropped bundle' when its cause is 'thieves', otherwise the record's label with its first letter upper-cased ('the communal store' becomes 'The communal store').
- one 'threat' marker for the active threat (state.features.threats.active) while its guard is below its guardNeeded, at its x and z, with id 'threat:' + threat id and a label naming its kind: 'Storm', 'Fire', 'Wolves' or 'Thieves'. There is none once guard reaches guardNeeded, or when no threat is active.
- one 'caravan' marker per view in selectCaravans(state), at the view's x and z (for a crate you commissioned, that is commissionPosition(crate, state.time)), with id 'caravan:' + view id and label the view's label (for example 'Your crate').

The in-game map draws these markers. Existing tests must keep passing.

items.title: Signature goods can be sent by caravan to the towns that wait for them
items.brief:
Commissioned caravan crates carry only ordinary resources. Signature goods, the only things milestone gates wait for, cannot be sent: every load has to be walked to the gate by hand, although the growth work promised the player could escort, commission and haul to speed towns up. A crate sold at a realm town also does not count as a haul for that town's standing or growth help, although handing a town foreign signature goods in person, or filling its order, does.

Required, for the caravans feature (actVillage(state, {type: 'feature', feature: 'caravans', action}); its state is state.features.caravans):
- Action {type: 'commission', from, to, good, amount}, where good is a signature good in the player's pack (state.features.economy.carried), sends a signature crate. It follows the same rules as a resource crate: the player within reach of the from-post (postPoint(from)); to among destinationsFrom(state, from); at most MAX_COMMISSIONS crates on the road; amount from 1 to MAX_COMMISSION_GOODS; fee commissionFee(from, to) paid in coins; departAt is the current time and arriveAt = departAt + (distance from dropPoint(from) to dropPoint(to)) / CARAVAN_SPEED + 4. The destination must be a realm settlement (never 'village'), and the pack must hold at least amount of that good; otherwise the action is refused and nothing changes. At dispatch the goods leave economy.carried. The crate is listed in state.features.caravans.commissions with its from, to, amount and good, and its view in selectCaravans(state) (id 'c.' + crate id, kind 'commission') has good set.
- On arrival, the destination settlement adds amount to signature.goods[good] and pays the player signaturePrice(settlement, good, 'sell') x amount, priced as the town stands just before the goods are added, out of its treasury, but never more than the treasury holds. The treasury falls by what is paid, and state.features.caravans.stats.earned rises by it. A 'commission' caravan deed for the destination is recorded in state.features.caravans.deeds, as today. When good is not the destination culture's own good, a 'delivered' reputation deed of that amount is also recorded for the destination (it appears in state.features.reputation.standings[town].deeds), as selling the goods there in person does, which also raises the town's help by 3 per unit.
- A resource crate sold at a realm settlement records a 'delivered' reputation deed for the amount sold (so the town's help rises by 3 per unit sold). Crates sold at Alder ('village') record no reputation deed (nothing is added to state.features.reputation.deedLog).
- A signature crate still on the road survives saveVillage and loadVillage with its from, to, good, amount and arrival time.
- At a caravan post, the loads the player can choose to send include the signature goods in their pack whenever the chosen destination is a realm settlement, with that town's price for them, and a signature crate on the road is listed by its good.

Existing caravans, economy and reputation tests must keep passing.

items.title: The idle director's sparks reach beyond Alder
items.brief:
When the player idles, the director offers one real need (a 'spark'), and the morning bell names the weightiest one. sparkCandidates(state) knows only Alder's projects, Alder's thin resource nodes and resource donations to a nearby town. It never points at a milestone gate you could feed with the signature goods you carry, at a settler waiting at your town for something, or at damage you could mend with what you carry, and destinationPoint cannot point at your town or at damage.

Required: sparkCandidates(state) also returns these sparks (each a Spark with id, label, verb, targetId, weight and isResolved):
- Gate sparks. For each known realm settlement (state.realm.settlements) whose centre (REALM_DEFS[id].center) is within 260 m of the player, and each signature good the player carries (state.features.economy.carried[good] > 0) that gateShortfall(settlement, lot) lists for an active lot there: a spark with id 'gate:' + settlement id + ':' + good, verb 'give', targetId 'warehouse:' + settlement id and weight 2. There is no spark for a good the player does not carry. Its isResolved(state) is true once no active lot there is short of that good, or the pack holds none of it.
- Settler sparks. For each candidate at your town (state.features.claimTown.town, a PlayerTown; its candidates) that has a home (homeId set) and a verdict whose band is not 'yes' and whose want is set: a spark with id 'settler:' + settlerId, verb 'build', targetId 'town:' + town id and weight 2, whose label contains the settler's name (as in SETTLER_DEFS) and wantText(want). It is resolved once that candidate is gone or their band is 'yes'.
- Repair sparks. For each damage record (DamageRecord) in state.features.threats.damage whose remaining needs (remainingNeeds(record)) the player's bag (state.inventory) covers in full (a record with nothing left to deliver always counts): a spark with id 'repair:' + record id, verb 'repair', targetId 'damage:' + record id and weight 3. It is resolved once the record is gone.
- destinationPoint(targetId, state) takes the game state as a new optional second argument and returns {x, z, label}: for 'town:<id>' your town's banner (the town's x and z), for 'damage:<id>' that record's x and z, and null when there is no such town or record. Every existing destination works as today, with or without the state. The DestinationId type admits both new forms, and Spark.targetId accepts them.
- Existing sparks, the seeded pick and the morning bell work as today: a fresh village still has no sparks, and morningBellMessage(state) returns the label of the highest-weight candidate.

Existing director tests must keep passing.

items.title: Neighbouring towns never build over your town or over pieces you placed
items.brief:
A founding stake only has to be 120 m from every settlement centre, but a frontier town's plan reaches about 125 m. From a legal stake 126 m out from Fernstead (frontier_0_1), up to 11 of Fernstead's planned parcels (fields, farm buildings, homes) lie within your town's radius, TOWN_RADIUS (36 m). When Fernstead grows, it raises buildings there, inside your town. Villages also start and finish buildings on top of pieces you placed: a fence standing on Alder North's unbuilt 'home' parcel does not stop Alder building its home there. Founding is not refused even when a neighbour's finished buildings already stand at the spot.

Required, for every realm settlement in state.realm.settlements (a lot's parcel centre is its x and z):
- Once your town is founded and the simulation has stepped (stepVillage), no settlement starts a lot (active true) or finishes one (tier above 0) whose parcel centre is within TOWN_RADIUS (inclusive) of your banner (state.features.claimTown.town x and z).
- Once a standing piece you placed is in state.features.building.pieces (a tuple whose last element, its condition, is above 0) and the simulation has stepped, no settlement starts or finishes a lot whose parcel centre is within 4 m (inclusive) of that piece's pieceCenter.
- Both rules hold for natural growth under stepVillage and for growRealmTo(state.realm, id, population). A lot finished before your town was founded, or before the piece was placed, stays, at no lower tier.
- The neighbour still grows everywhere else. With a fence on one of its planned home parcels, Fernstead grown to 600 has more than 150 finished lots. Grown to 1,000 beside your town, it keeps its 1,000 people.
- Founding, actVillage(state, {type: 'feature', feature: 'claimTown', action: {type: 'plant', choice}}), is refused when a finished lot (tier above 0) of any realm settlement is within TOWN_RADIUS of the stake spot. Refused means actVillage returns the same state object and state.features.claimTown.town stays null. Every existing refusal stays, and a legal spot with no finished lot within TOWN_RADIUS is still accepted. plantBlockedReason, given the terrain module's walkable, accepts and refuses the same spots as today: a spot it accepts beside a neighbour's finished lot is refused when the stake is planted there. While the stake is held, the founding chip does not offer to plant at a spot that planting would refuse for this reason.

The situations that must hold:
- Stakes are planted as today, 3 m ahead of the player: state.features.claimTown.stake is 'held', and the player stands at the spot's x and at its z + 3, with yaw 0. A spot is legal when plantBlockedReason({...createClaimTown(), stake: 'held'}, x, z, walkable) returns '' (walkable is the terrain module's).
- Town radius: take the legal point 126 m from getRealmDefinition('frontier_0_1').center, over angles in 5-degree steps, with the most settlementPlan parcels (homes, crafts, market, farm, wells and named) within 36 m. On a new village (createVillage) with frontier_0_1 discovered (discoverRealm), found the town there, step 2 s, and grow frontier_0_1 to 1,000. Neither then nor after stepping 180 s more is any lot within 36 m of the banner started or finished.
- Pieces on a village's first sites: on a new village, fences go at the parcel centres of Alder North's 'home' lot and Willowbank's 'storehouse' lot, both unbuilt. Through six steps of 20 s, no lot within 4 m of either fence is started or finished.
- Pieces on a neighbour's future parcel: on a new village, a fence goes at the centre of settlementPlan(frontier_0_1).homes[9]. After stepping 2 s and growing frontier_0_1 to 600, no lot within 4 m of it is started or finished. A second fence then goes on one of Fernstead's finished homes more than 30 m from its centre. After stepping 10 s, that home is still there at no lower tier.
- A fence is the tuple [PIECE_IDS.indexOf('fence'), Math.round(x - 0.5), Math.round(z), 0, 0, 2], set directly in state.features.building.pieces. Its pieceCenter is ({kind: 'fence', x: tuple[1], z: tuple[2], rotation: 0}).
- Refusal: on a new village stepped 2 s with frontier_0_1 grown to 600, take a legal spot within 35 m of one of Fernstead's finished lots. Planting there is refused. Then take a legal spot 170 m from Fernstead's centre, more than 37 m from every finished lot. Planting there is accepted, and the town stands at that spot.

Existing realms, plan, growth, claimTown and building tests must keep passing.

items.title: Join any job, including in the towns you visit
items.brief:
'Join any job' (tap in rhythm with someone at work) only works with Alder's eight residents. The workers of the towns you visit cannot be joined, even when they are gathering, crafting or building right in front of you.

Required, for the 'director' feature:
- Its interaction targets, as listed by featureTargets(state), include a point for each realm worker (state.realm.settlements[settlement id].workers) within 20 m of the player (state.player) whose task.phase is 'work' and whose task.kind is 'gather', 'craft' or 'build'. The point has id 'feature:director:job:' + settlement id + ':' + worker id, name 'Join ' + the worker's name, action 'Join', and x and z at the worker's position. A worker further than 20 m away, not in phase 'work', or on any other kind of task has no point. Activating the point, featureInteraction(state, point id), gives feature 'director' and the action {type: 'jobTap', realmId: settlement id, workerId: worker id}.
- The action {type: 'jobTap', realmId, workerId}, dispatched with actVillage(state, {type: 'feature', feature: 'director', action}), follows the rules for taps on Alder's residents:
  - It is refused, with the reason 'There is no work to join there right now.' (as read by takeFeatureRejection()), unless that worker is at work (task.phase 'work') on a 'gather', 'craft' or 'build' task.
  - A tap less than 0.22 s of game time (state.time) after the last accepted tap on the same worker is refused.
  - A refused tap changes nothing: actVillage returns the state it was given.
  - scoreJobTiming(state.time) (beat JOB_BEAT_SECONDS = 1.4) decides the effect: 'perfect' takes 1.2 s off the worker's task.remaining, 'good' takes 0.6 s, and 'miss' does nothing. remaining never goes below 0.
- A good run with one worker (3 or more taps, at least 60% of them not misses) records a 'delivered' reputation deed of amount 1 for the worker's settlement (it appears in state.features.reputation.standings[settlement id].deeds), which also raises that settlement's help (state.realm.settlements[settlement id].help) by 3. This happens at most once per worker per game day (selectClock(state).day), even if the worker starts a new task that day.
- Taps on Alder's residents ({type: 'jobTap', npcId}) and their targets ('feature:director:job:' + npc id, activating to {type: 'jobTap', npcId}) behave as today.

All of this holds in a game started with createVillage() and advanced with stepVillage() between taps, including when state.player, state.time and a worker's task fields (phase, kind, remaining) are set directly.

Existing director tests must keep passing.
